snippet.title: DanDoesData MadeUp or Startup? #3 Basic GAN
snippet.description: We finally setup a basic generator-discriminator loop!  After massaging the data into the right format and changing the name length (to help balance the character classes), we can start training.  Next time we'll try to randomize and optimize the training a bit better ad reflect on this simple GAN.   -- Watch live at https://www.twitch.tv/vanboxel

snippet.title: DanDoesData MadeUp or Startup? #2: Convolutional Sequence
snippet.description: We change up the LSTM model to a 1D convolution of fixed output size to better match what we want to put into the GAN.  No training here, but we put together the generator model as well as a simple encoder to pretrain it a little bit.  Next week some actual training and hopefully developing the discriminator model.   -- Watch live at https://www.twitch.tv/vanboxel

snippet.title: DanDoesData MadeUp or Startup? #1 Name Generator
snippet.description: MadeUp or StartUp?  We're building a system to generate real-sounding startup names.  This episode introduces the dataset and walks through a previous language model that can generate names.  The old model still works!  Wouldn't you like to join,"Fiend Social"?   -- Watch live at https://www.twitch.tv/vanboxel

snippet.title: DanDoesData Poutyne! PyTorch Simplified
snippet.description: Poutyne is a front-end library for the popular PyTorch machine learning framework.  It provides an interface similar to Keras...once you have a basic Torch network put together.  The problem I encountered is that Torch has weird strong opinions about their models and loss functions, making it seem impossible to surmount.  I can already do what I need in TensorFlow and Keras, so it's not worth to me to learn another tool to do the same thing.  Shame for PyTorch.  But if you're stuck with that library, Poutyne is a great way to simplify the training process.   -- Watch live at https://www.twitch.tv/vanboxel

snippet.title: DanDoesData PyTorch: Reforged
snippet.description: We take a fresh look at PyTorch, a competing ML library similar to TensorFlow or the old Theano.  It's made a lot of great progress and is in some ways better than TF.  But there also seems to be object-oriented solutions forced into a situation that doesn't warrant it. Thankfully, we also have `poutyne`!   -- Watch live at https://www.twitch.tv/vanboxel

snippet.title: DanDoesData John Snow's Cholera Map Recreation
snippet.description: We recreate John Snow's famous 1854 map of cholera deaths.  This map helped researchers understand that cholera was in fact due to bad water, in this case centered on the Broad St pump in London.   -- Watch live at https://www.twitch.tv/vanboxel

snippet.title: DanDoesData MNIST Mash #5 Convolution Neural Network
snippet.description: We've futzed around enough, it's time to build a decent model using proven methods: Convolutional Neural Networks for image recognition.   -- Watch live at https://www.twitch.tv/vanboxel

snippet.title: DanDoesData MNIST Mash #4 Linear Models and More
snippet.description: We create a simple linear model based on the pixel inputs and note that it does better than the simple heuristic.  But, creating a neural net quickly stalls as the model predicts identical values no matter the input.  More to come.   -- Watch live at https://www.twitch.tv/vanboxel

snippet.title: DanDoesData MNIST Mash #3 Heuristic
snippet.description: We build a very simple heuristic model as a baseline to compare to the dopey ML model. -- Watch live at https://www.twitch.tv/vanboxel

snippet.title: DanDoesData MNIST Mash #2 Mean Data
snippet.description: Discovery and fixing of a data error as well as trying an heuristic. -- Watch live at https://www.twitch.tv/vanboxel

snippet.title: DanDoesData MNIST Mash #1 Extraction Data Creation
snippet.description: MNIST is too easy; let's make it harder by smashing digits on top of each other.  To do that, we'll need to make a fresh dataset from the original MNIST, taking digits and correctly grabbing their labels.  GitHub repo: https://github.com/dvbuntu/mnist_mash -- Watch live at https://www.twitch.tv/vanboxel

snippet.title: DanDoesData TensorFlow 2.1.0
snippet.description: Return of DanDoesData!  And as usual, TensorFlow is disagreeable.  Will our hero have to turn to other libraries?  Tune in next week to find out! -- Watch live at https://www.twitch.tv/vanboxel

snippet.title: The End of DanDoesData: Self-driving car sabbatical
snippet.description: Going on sabbatical, so let's spend one last stream looking at the self-driving car.  And build a half-way decent model!

snippet.title: Line By Line Keras Examples 2
snippet.description: Examining a curious MNIST example, using an RNN on the pixels to predict the digit.

snippet.title: LinebyLine Keras Examples 1
snippet.description: Let's walk through several of the Keras machine learning examples at https://github.com/fchollet/keras/tree/master/examples, line by line.

snippet.title: DanDoesData Project Euler P3-4
snippet.description: More working through project Euler, starting from problem 3

snippet.title: DanDoesData Project Euler
snippet.description: Taking a break from machine learning, let's work through some of the challenges on Project Euler.  Starting with Python, then maybe C++, or possibly even Fortran. Problems 1-3 (still working on number3)

snippet.title: Bardic Lore: Kid's Stories
snippet.description: Having found a couple corpora of children's literature from various authors, we'll see how the "train gradually more complex models" plan works.

snippet.title: Bardic Lore: Transfer Learning
snippet.description: Now that we have a model that does something, let's redo this, starting with simple models.  Then we use the weights from those to kickstart more complex models.  Ideally, we'd do this with more complex data, but I didn't find a suitable dataset in time.

snippet.title: Bardic Lore: Improved Model
snippet.description: The previously trained RNN model spit out lots of spaces; I think we can fix that with a little more preprocessing and get a model that does something intelligent.

snippet.title: Dan Does Data Keras 2 Launch Stream
snippet.description: Keras 2 just came out (https://blog.keras.io/introducing-keras-2.html), so let's upgrade and see what all is new.  And how much of my old code breaks.  We'll work through some classic examples and work on the current Bardic Lore text generation project.

snippet.title: Bardic Lore: Regenerating Shakespeare
snippet.description: char-rnn is all the rage for generating text these days, but let's roll our own text generation service using Keras and various recurrent neural networks.  Because we already have Shakespeare handy, let's see if we can awake the spirit of the Bard.

snippet.title: DanDoesData TensorFlow 1.0 and TFLearn
snippet.description: TensorFlow 1.0 is out!  While that comes with lots of changes, I wanted to look at the high-level interface via "TFLearn".  I was a big fan of `skflow`, but that's out, so let's see what TFLearn can do.

snippet.title: DanDoesData Valentine's Day Special
snippet.description: On this very special Valentine's Day, we're going to look through dating profiles from the https://github.com/rudeboybert/JSE_OkCupid data set.

snippet.title: DanDoesData Leaf Disease more modeling
snippet.description: Ongoing study of the leaf disease problem.  We're going to focus on reformatting the data and working with compressed images.  Thanks again to Nerd Farmer for sponsoring!

snippet.title: DanDoesData: Convolutional Autoencoders
snippet.description: We take a crack at convolutional  autocoders.  It starts easy, but handling goofy sizes takes a little more finesse.

snippet.title: PyTorch Installation and Intro
snippet.description: Torch has been around as a machine learning framework for awhile now, but it only recently came out with Python bindings.  Let's see how it measures up to the competition.

snippet.title: GrowMobile Plant Disease Classification
snippet.description: Looking at a new dataset tonight: images of leaves that may or may not be diseased.  Let's see if we can put together a basic model.  Data is from CrowdAI and this episode is sponsored by GrowMobile, LLC and NerdFarmer.

snippet.title: Self-driving car Nvidia Autopilot implementation
snippet.description: We'll be implementing the Nvidia Autopilot model (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1604.07316.pdf, as seen https://github.com/SullyChen/Autopilot-TensorFlow) and seeing how it does on our limited dataset.  Likely, we're going to learn that the secret sauce is the mountains of data.

snippet.title: Bare Minimum: Matplotlib for data visualization
snippet.description: When physical distance equals logical distance, insight happens.  This is the first in a "Bare Minimum" series where I'll explain and demonstrate some minimal useful tool or method.  Today's tool is matplotlib, a wonderful tool for plotting things in Python.  But you only really need to know scatter plots and heat maps to solve most problems.

snippet.title: Dan Does Data: All About Autoencoders
snippet.description: What do you do when you don't have enough labeled data?  Autoencoding is a way to learn (hopefully interesting) features of your data to save time on training later.  Let's explore!  And only crash my machine once during the show...

snippet.title: Dan Does Data Interactive Computing Workflow
snippet.description:
By popular request, this livestream will demonstrate setting up and using my interactive computing workflow.  Learn how to do data science (or whatever!) with Ubuntu, Tmux, ViM, and Slimux.  Feel the Power!

If you're downloading the repo, make sure to select the 'ubuntu' branch.  The 'master' branch is for ArchLinux.  If you're using Arch, you probably already know what to do.

snippet.title: Dan Does Data: IPython Notebooks with SageMathCloud
snippet.description: While I usually stick with ViM and IPython in the terminal, many folks enjoy data science in IPython Notebooks (or JuPyter).  Conveniently, SageMathCloud makes these available in tiny VMs with all kinds of pre-installed libraries.  Let's Learn.

snippet.title: CNTK Revisited: Now with Python
snippet.description: CNTK is a machine learning framework from Microsoft that came out awhile ago, but I recently saw that they updated it with Python bindings.  I said I would give it another look if they did, so let's see what's new!

snippet.title: DanDoesData TensorFlow Anniversary!
snippet.description: Let's celebration one year of TensorFlow and DanDoesData!  What better way to do it than reinstalling TensorFlow!

snippet.title: Intro to Google DataStudio
snippet.description: Google Datastudio looks like a flexible web app for doing exploratory data science.  Let's see how it handles...

snippet.title: Self-driving car data collection platform
snippet.description: With Otto, the self-driving tractor in some state of "working", it's time to start collecting proper data.  This is the creation of a script to read from the webcam and FUBARino board, process things into the right format, and spit out the data as .npz files.

snippet.title: Self-driving car with basic RNN
snippet.description: "What's past is prologue."  Let's try to implement a simple recurrent neural network.  In this way, we include features computed at a previous time step in the current step's computation.  We do get a model running here, but it's not clear that it's giving us additional predictive power.

snippet.title: Self-driving car Model Review
snippet.description: Mostly a review of some off-camera modeling.  SqueezeNet Transfer learning (a bust so far), building the DeepDrive model in Keras (lists to the left), and a venture into Linear modeling (causing a literal computer crash at the end, sorry!).

snippet.title: Self-driving car Transfer Learning Model
snippet.description: Trying to train our own entire model is a challenge, especially with limited data.  What if we can use part of an existing model (including weights) to extract most of the important features, then finish the job ourselves?

snippet.title: Self-driving Car Comma.ai model
snippet.description: More modeling with the comma.ai self-driving car data set.  And I managed to crash my computer half-way through; sorry about the short episode.

snippet.title: Self-driving Car Comma.ai dataset
snippet.description: Let's try some new data, the recently released Comma.Ai dataset (https://github.com/commaai/research) looks interesting.  We can see how the DeepDrive trained model performs, and vice versa.

snippet.title: Self-driving Car Control script (and viewer model)
snippet.description: We go over the control script used by the machine learning model to communicate and direct the car over a serial port.  We also take a look at a viewer submitted model that beats what I concocted last week :p  If you've got a better model still, send it in!

snippet.title: Self-driving car Combined model
snippet.description: With the compressed data model working ok, it's time to focus on building a model good enough to drive with.  It's time for either a combined model of steering and gas, or at least two models.

snippet.title: Self-driving car Building a smaller model with regularization
snippet.description: The deadline for this Self-driving car is approaching.  This week we'll use a compressed version of the data to save a lot of preprocessing effort.  Today's motto, "This is fine."

snippet.title: Self-driving Car Visualization and Gas Model
snippet.description: More self-driving car modeling.  Now with a sweet animation of the steering!  We start work on the gas model, converting to categorical variables, but predicting "always drive forward" is too good for the model to overcome.

snippet.title: Self-driving Car Autonomous Steering
snippet.description: With a basic autonomous model doing...something, let's do something simpler: focus on steering angle.  Modeling this should be easy, visualizing it shouldn't be too bad either.

snippet.title: Self-driving car Parameter Rescaling
snippet.description: Ongoing modeling of a self-driving car for Power Racing Series FUBAR team.  This time we tackle a model that's outputting all zeros or constants!  Rescaling and new activations to the rescue.

snippet.title: Self-driving car DeepDrive model
snippet.description: Extracting the necessary data out of the DeepDrive dataset and training a simple model for a self driving car, if all goes well.

snippet.title: Self-driving car DeepDrive data inspection
snippet.description: Ongoing modeling of Powerwheels Racing self-driving car.  Github repo at https://github.com/dvbuntu/autonomous.  Still looking for a good dataset, but deepdrive.io is a decent start.  Unfortunately, the images look a bit off color.  Maybe they're not RGB like I thought.

snippet.title: Self-driving car model setup
snippet.description: FUBAR Labs is part of the Powerwheels Racing autonomous challenge.  I'm setting up and building a model to teach a go-kart how to drive.  No data yet, just specifications and ideas.  Github repo at https://github.com/dvbuntu/autonomous

snippet.title: For Well Thou Know'st: CNN/RNN Combo
snippet.description: An RNN was cool, but feeding it better scale features from a convolutional layer is even cooler.

snippet.title: For Well Thou Know'st: Recurrent prep
snippet.description:
Last week I was off, but I published a TensorFlow video series!  https://www.packtpub.com/big-data-and-business-intelligence/deep-learning-tensorflow-video

Having crafted a decent, if expensive, convolutional model, I seek to building a simpler recurrent model to slowly build up confidence in a class.

snippet.title: For Well Thou Kn: Non-cheating model
snippet.description: Armed with a revised data set of The Bard, I hope to model fonts without cheating.

snippet.title: For Well Thou Kn: New Data
snippet.description: After modeling the old data with just a couple features, it seems wise to redo the data set to ensure we're actually capturing the features we want.

snippet.title: For Well Thou Kn: Minimal features
snippet.description: Ongoing study of Shakespeare's text, literally studying fonts.  This week we'll see how few features we can use on this particular data.

snippet.title: For Well Thou Kn: Simple Models
snippet.description: Ongoing explorations of the works of William Shakespeare, and beyond.  We succeed in building a simple logistic regression and even a shallow neural network.  Github page at https://github.com/dvbuntu/for_well_thou_kn

snippet.title: DanDoesData Reading in Shakespeare Data
snippet.description: Enough with every framework under the sun, it's time for a new research project.  Tonight, we create and read in a dataset of Shakespeare rendered in a variety of fonts.  "For well thou know'st".  Code and more information on Github, https://github.com/dvbuntu/for_well_thou_kn.

snippet.title: DanDoesData Caffe Segfault
snippet.description: Continuing study of caffe.  Though I was able to load the docker container for caffe, all of the intro models caused docker to crash.  I'm done with caffe for now as a result.

snippet.title: DanDoesData Caffe Installation and Compiling
snippet.description: We're moving on to Caffe, another popular framework.  This one is tricky to install; I gave up and switched docker after streaming.

snippet.title: LineByLine TensorFlow mnist.py
snippet.description: A Statistically Responsible look at the mnist.py TensorFlow tutorial file.

snippet.title: LineByLine: TensorFlow fully_connected_feed.py
snippet.description:
A new series, "Line by Line", where I'll walk through an example tutorial (maybe my own, maybe existing) line by line, explaining and running the code.

First up, by fan request, is a TensorFlow tutorial on fully connected neural nets.

snippet.title: DanDoesData Simple RNNs in Keras
snippet.description:
We finally get an RNN working for the word embeddings model.  The key is you supply single sentences to the model, not all the data at once!

Then I whipped up a semi-fake model to predict the season based on temperature.  It really seems to like Autumn, but the important thing is that it's easy to run and understand.  Built with a simple Long Short Term Memory model.

snippet.title: DanDoesData Keras 1.0 and more RNN
snippet.description: Keras 1.0 came out, woo!  And we try our luck again with Recurrent Neural Networks, but maybe I picked a bad initial problem.

snippet.title: DanDoesData Keras Recurrent Neural Nets
snippet.description:
We're going to continue looking at Keras, but also at Recurrent Neural Nets and maybe LSTMs.  It's about time.

Of course, these aren't trivial to jump into!  And there's no Keras examples of Simple RNNs, so we try to shim in a Theano example.  You decide how well it went...

snippet.title: DanDoesData Trailer
snippet.description: What is DanDoesData?  Find out and see some highlights from the past few months!

snippet.title: DanDoesData Special Edition: Excel97
snippet.description: We're going to examine a highly versatile machine learning framework put out by Microsoft, Excel97!.  It features a more graphical scripting approach, and is usable by anyone!  No programming experience required.

snippet.title: DanDoesData Keras Custom Activations and Convolutions
snippet.description:
In this video, I figured out how to implement custom Keras activations!  This is useful in case the library falls behind the latest machine learning research.  Maybe our custom arctan(X) + sin(X) function will take the world by storm and get implemented proper in Keras.

I also demonstrate how to do convolutional layers in Keras.  They make it pretty easy, so you don't need to stress too much about it.

snippet.title: Dan Does Data Keras Intro
snippet.description: Tonight we'll be exploring another high-level wrapper library, Keras.  This one is unique in that it supports both Theano and TensorFlow backends.

snippet.title: DanDoesData CIFAR10 in skflow with convolutional net
snippet.description: Building a CIFAR-10 image recognition model with skflow.  After wrestling with importing data last time, we're finally ready to do some actual modeling.  Also, pretty pictures of weights from the red, green, and blue color channels!

snippet.title: DanDoesData CIFAR10 with skflow reading data
snippet.description:
CIFAR10 intro with skflow.  This was a bear to just start reading in data.  The TensorFlow documentation doesn't expect you to want to look at an image yourself it seems.  So I rolled my own using numpy and at least made a simple logistic model with skflow.  To create the proper convolutional neural net, we need to rearrange our data into [n_samples, height, width, n_channels] format.  That's a future video.

As usual, 5 minutes of silent research showed me that np.transpose will reorder the data, and I can view an rgb numpy array with plt.imshow(foo).  Things are looking up for next time!

snippet.title: DanDoesData Uncovering skflow custom weights
snippet.description: TensorFlow 0.7 wheel doesn't work with Python3 yet (welcome to dependency hell).  So I reinstalled TF 0.6.  In the end, we will find the hidden weights in the dark heart of TensorFlow.

snippet.title: Dan Does Data SciKit Flow (skflow) weights
snippet.description: This week we'll be delving deeper into the skflow interface to TensorFlow.  We visualize some of the weights of our Convolutional Neural Net and strike deep into the heart of `classifier.get_tensor_value` to recover additional weights.  Plus, we spend the last 5 minutes reinstalling tensorflow!

snippet.title: DanDoesData Live in Person at FUBARLabs
snippet.description: Broadcasting from FUBAR Labs, I hosted a workshop on "Data Visualization and Machine Learning".   We used SageMathCloud, so you can try this on any machine!  Check out the IPython Notebook used in the class at https://github.com/dvbuntu/ml_workshop/blob/master/ml_workshop.ipynb

snippet.title: DanDoesData TensorFlow with skflow
snippet.description: This week I'll look at a high-level wrapping language around Tensorflow called "skflow".  It makes building neural networks super easy.  While they advertise it as an "educational" tool, this is an "educational" show, so we can use it as much as we like!

snippet.title: DanDoesData Theano CNN Visualizations
snippet.description:
I persevere applying Convolutional Neural Nets in Python using Theano, with some visualization of the weights and even a few neural network "dreams" of random data made into digits.  I will walk through a simple example with MNIST digits to demonstrate what each layer of a traditional CNN does (convolution layer, pooling layer, and what it all means).

Based on tutorial at https://github.com/Newmu/Theano-Tutorials/blob/master/5_convolutional_net.py

snippet.title: DanDoesData: Theano Convolutional Neural Net Intro
snippet.description: We're continuing to explore Theano, this time looking at Convolutional Neural Nets (CNNs).  CNNs are great at reducing your parameter count and finding features located anywhere in your [image, sound pattern, text] or other structured data.

snippet.title: Dan Does Data: Microsoft CNTK new Deep Learning library!
snippet.description:
Now it's Microsoft's turn to see me flop through their newly released tool.  Props to them for releasing a Linux version alongside Windows.

Pre-compiled binaries don't seem to be available yet, so you'll see me try to compile from source.  I was able to use their old codeplex CPU-only release eventually. When they release new Linux binaries (and maybe python bindings), I'll give CNTK a fresh look.

More info about my workflow at https://dvbuntu.github.io/compute.  General blog and data science critiques at https://dvbuntu.github.io/wisdom.

snippet.title: DanDoesData: Theano Deep MLP for MNIST
snippet.description: We'll continue learning how to break Theano by building a simple neural net to classify handwritten digits in the MNIST dataset.  And we expand on the deeplearning.net tutorial by creating a class for an arbitrary number of hidden layers.  See if I can pull myself up out of bugs of my own creation!

snippet.title: Dan Does Data, Theano MNIST Logistic Regression
snippet.description:
See me fail to copy-paste correctly and misimplement a simple logistic regression model.  All the digits are one's, right?

As usual, 15 minutes of debugging located my error.  I overwrote the `updates` list instead of adding another entry for the bias value.  So I got burned by not having a simple concatenate operator to add my bias feature to the pixels.  Oh well.  Next week, we'll use an actual neural net.

Just an engineer stumbling through machine learning and other software tutorials.  Watch me fumble through confusing installations, unintuitive interfaces, and a hostile computing environment.  And yet somehow, I'll manage to analyze data (with some probability).
